# Repertoire stability {#stability}

This chapter covers the **paired (longitudinal) comparisons**, where the same
subjects were sampled at two timepoints. Stability is measured as **Kulczynski
similarity** between samples, split into two sets of pairs:

- **Within individual**: a subject's first timepoint against their own second
  timepoint, one pair per subject.
- **Between individuals**: every pair of samples from two different subjects.

Comparing the two sets asks whether a person's antibody repertoire is a stable
personal signature, or drifts so much that two timepoints of the same person
look no more alike than samples of different people. Unpaired comparisons
contrast different people, so they have no within-individual pairs and no
stability page.

```{r, results='asis'}
stable <- Filter(function(x) isTRUE(x$stability), book$comparisons)
if (!length(stable)) {
  cat(no_plot("No comparison has stability: true in report_config.yml."), "\n\n")
}

for (cmp in stable) {
  base <- file.path(cmp_base(cmp), "similarity")
  cat(cmp_heading(cmp, 1, "stability"))
  cat(cmp_intro(cmp))

  cat("## Within- vs between-individual similarity\n\n")
  cat(similarity_block(cmp), "\n\n")
  cat("### Distribution\n\n")
  cat(nox_img(file.path(base, "kulczynski_boxplot.svg"), paste("Similarity distribution:", cmp$label)), "\n\n")
  cat("### Combined view\n\n")
  cat(nox_img(file.path(base, "kulczynski_combined.svg"), paste("Combined similarity view:", cmp$label)), "\n\n")
  cat("### Pairwise similarity heatmap\n\n")
  cat(callout(paste("Each cell is one sample pair. Paired timepoints of the same subject form a",
                    "bright diagonal when repertoires are individually stable.")), "\n\n")
  cat(nox_img(file.path(base, "kulczynski_heatmap.svg"), paste("Similarity heatmap:", cmp$label)), "\n\n")

  cat("## DELTA outcome\n\n")
  n <- delta_counts(cmp)
  if (is.na(n[["passing"]]) || n[["passing"]] == 0) {
    cat(callout(sprintf(paste("<strong>No DELTA features</strong> with m<sub>eff</sub> &gt; %s and",
                              "p_perm &lt; 0.05 in this comparison."), book$delta$min_m_eff), "none"), "\n\n")
  } else {
    cat(n[["passing"]], " features pass the DELTA filter; see the [DELTA overview](#delta-summary-",
        cmp$id, ").\n\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```
